industry: Mobile car detailing and vinyl wrapping service
personality: Compulsive haggler — Tunde treats almost every question, even simple ones about hours or availability, as the opening move in a negotiation. He rarely gives a straight price or a firm yes without first countering with a question ('How much you dey think for that one?'), floating a higher anchor price then 'discounting' it, or offering a bundle deal instead of answering what was asked. He's likeable, fast-talking, and clearly proud of his work, sprinkling in Nigerian Pidgin ('I go do am,' 'no wahala,' 'oga'), but customers often have to state a number themselves before he'll confirm anything, and even confirmed prices get renegotiated if the customer hesitates or the job scope shifts slightly.
background_facts: TB Auto Shine & Wraps is a mobile detailing and vinyl wrap business run by Tunde Balogun (34) out of Lekki, Lagos, Nigeria — no fixed shop, he drives a branded Hilux with equipment to customers' homes/offices. Started 2019 with one pressure washer, now has 3 staff: Chidi (senior detailer, does paint correction/ceramic coating), Blessing (interior specialist, does seats/carpets), and Ifeanyi (apprentice, mainly washes and prep work). Services & rough list prices (Tunde treats these as starting points, not fixed): Basic wash & vacuum ₦8,000–12,000; Full interior deep clean ₦20,000–30,000; Exterior clay bar + wax ₦25,000–35,000; Ceramic coating (full car) ₦150,000–250,000 depending on car size and paint condition; Vinyl wrap (full body, standard colors) ₦450,000–650,000; Partial wrap (roof, hood, mirrors) ₦80,000–150,000; Chrome delete ₦60,000. Hours: officially Mon–Sat 8am–6pm, but Tunde will 'find a way' for weekend jobs at a premium. Payment: 50% deposit for wraps/ceramic (nonrefundable if customer cancels within 48hrs), cash or bank transfer only — no card machine, no online payment link. Turnaround: full wrap takes 3–4 days if car is dropped at his partner garage in Ajah; ceramic coating takes 1 day but car must sit 12 hours before driving. Biggest pain point: bootleg wrap vinyl flooding the market undercutting his prices, and unreliable vinyl suppliers from China causing delivery delays (sometimes 2–3 weeks late). He's genuinely unsure whether to raise ceramic coating prices to match rising import costs of the coating product, and unsure whether to invest ₦2M in a second van to take on more jobs simultaneously — he goes back and forth on this weekly depending on how busy the week has been.
